To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AFS Convention significantly reduced the concentrations of TBT in surface water, while it had little effect on TPhT.
the AFS convention has significantly improved the water quality in the TGR; however, the sediment still poses a potential risk to the aquatic community in the TGR and human health.
the AFS Convention implementation and water level fluctuations in a freshwater reservoir significantly affected the distribution, transport, and risk of TBT and its alternative TPhT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pollution evolution of TBT and its replacement compound TPhT in a large reservoir.

the pollution evolution processes and risk assessment of organotin compounds in the TGR after implementation of the Convention, which provides a scientific basis for further management of organotins in the TGRR.
the pollution evolution of TBT and the potential health risk of TPhT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the AFS Convention has effectively reduced the pollution levels of TBT and especially TPhT in water and fish in the TGR; however, the pollution levels of both TBTs in the sediment are still very high.
TBT and TphT in the TGT are not a serious threat, but the risks cannot be ignored.
the TBT and TphT pollution in the TGR has not been eliminated after implementation of the Convention, but has been controlled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water level regulation of TGR significantly affected TBT and TphT fate, transfer and transport in the TGR.
water level fluctuation should be considered in the risk assessment and management of TBT and other organotins in the TGR.
water level regulation of TGR is an important factor affecting the fate and transport of TPhT and TBT in the TGR.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the implementation of the AfsC is effective, and it is necessary to continue to monitor and assess the pollution evolution processes and risks of TBT and other pollutants to ensure the sustainable development of the TGRR.
the water level regulation in the TGR significantly affects the fate and transport of organotins in the TGR and should be taken into consideration when evaluating organotin pollution in the TGRR.
the AFS Convention can effectively reduce the input of TBT and its degradation products into the environment.
